services.name: Eldercare Locator
services.description: Free help finding care for an older parent or relative, and support for the person caring for them.
services.hours: Mon to Fri, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. Eastern
services.eligibility: Anyone caring for an older adult, or an older adult looking for help.

steps: Call 1-800-677-1116, or search by ZIP code at eldercare.acl.gov.
Ask who helps caregivers in your county.

services.name: Sinclair Student Food Pantry
services.description: Free food supplies for Sinclair students.
services.eligibility: Sinclair students who need food.

steps: Go to Building 13, Room 426.
Check sinclair.edu/foodpantry for open dates.

services.name: Lunch Time Hunger Program
services.description: Free lunch, no questions asked.
services.hours: Monday to Thursday, 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.
services.eligibility: Sinclair students. No questions asked.

steps: Walk in during lunch hours.

services.name: Sinclair Student Assistance Request (case management)
services.description: Someone on staff calls you back. They help with housing, food, or health needs, and they know who else can help.
services.eligibility: Sinclair students facing housing, food, or health needs.

steps: Fill out the Student Assistance Request form.
A staff member will contact you.

services.name: Sinclair Student Emergency Grant
services.description: One-time money for an emergency, like rent, food, a bill, or internet.
services.eligibility: Enrolled at least 6 credit hours this semester in a degree or certificate program, with a documented emergency. GPA, aid status and past awards may be considered. Once while at Sinclair.

steps: Get a paper that shows the need, like a late bill.
Apply through the link on sinclair.edu/emergencygrant.
documents: Proof of the emergency (bill, notice, or estimate)

services.name: Raider Food Pantry
services.description: Free emergency food for Wright State students, by appointment, once a month.
services.eligibility: Wright State students enrolled this term who need emergency food.

steps: Book an appointment online with your campus login (no walk-ins).
Arrive on time; more than 5 minutes late without notice cancels the appointment.

services.name: Apply for SNAP, cash or child care help
services.description: The state's online form for SNAP food help, cash help, and help paying for child care.

organization.name: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services

services.eligibility: There are rules about income and who lives with you. Most students who take six or more credits also need to meet one extra rule, like working 20 hours a week.

steps: Create an account at benefits.ohio.gov.
Fill out the application.
Complete the interview when the county calls.
Send any verification they ask for.
documents: Proof of income for the last 30 days
Proof of the student exemption (work schedule, work-study award, or child care need)

services.name: Montgomery County Job and Family Services
services.description: The county office for SNAP, cash, Medicaid and child care assistance.
services.eligibility: Montgomery County residents.

steps: Apply online at benefits.ohio.gov, or visit or call the office.

services.name: Greene County Job and Family Services
services.description: The county office for SNAP, cash, Medicaid and publicly funded child care.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents.

steps: Apply online at benefits.ohio.gov.
For Medicaid you can also call 1-844-640-6446.

services.name: Ohio HEAP heating assistance
services.description: Help with winter heating bills for households with lower income. You can apply from July 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027. It can take up to twelve weeks.
services.eligibility: Household income at or below 175% of poverty.

steps: Apply online at energyhelp.ohio.gov. Or set up a time with Miami Valley Community Action Partnership.
documents: List of household members and proof of income for each adult
Most recent gas and electric bills
Birth dates and Social Security numbers for household members
Proof of disability, if it applies

services.name: Miami Valley Community Action Partnership
services.description: A local agency that helps with bills. This is where you set up a time to apply for heating help.
services.eligibility: Income rules vary by program.

steps: Call to ask which programs fit and to make an appointment.

services.name: The Foodbank pantry locator
services.description: The food bank for this area. Look up pantries by ZIP code, or find a mobile pantry near you.
services.eligibility: Varies by pantry.

steps: Search the pantry locator by ZIP code.
Call the pantry to confirm hours and what to bring.

services.name: 2-1-1 Helpline
services.description: Free, confidential help finding food, paying bills and other services.

organization.name: United Way of the Greater Dayton Area

services.eligibility: Anyone.

services.name: House of Bread
services.description: Hot lunch every day of the year.
services.hours: Daily, 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., 365 days a year
services.eligibility: Anyone in need.

steps: Walk in during lunch.

services.name: Good Neighbor House
services.description: A drive-thru food pantry. They also have a clinic for health care and teeth.
services.hours: Drive-thru pantry Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.; call first
services.eligibility: Call to speak with an intake volunteer.

steps: Call first to speak with an intake volunteer.

services.name: St. Vincent de Paul of Dayton
services.description: A place to stay tonight, help finding housing, food, clothes, and things for your home.

organization.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Dayton

services.eligibility: Call or visit the website for current intake.

steps: Visit stvincentdayton.org or call for shelter intake.

services.name: Catholic Social Services Choice Food Pantry
services.description: Choice food pantry with case management for west and northwest Dayton residents.

organization.name: Catholic Social Services of the Miami Valley

services.eligibility: For people who live in west and northwest Dayton. Call and ask for 1101 to see if you can use it.

steps: Call 937-223-7217, ext. 1101, to see if you can use it.

services.name: Have A Gay Day Community Food Pantry
services.description: A food pantry that can also bring food to you.
services.eligibility: Call for current hours and delivery.

steps: Call or visit the website.

services.name: Greene County FISH Pantry
services.description: Food pantry; one visit every four weeks. Second and fourth Saturdays 8 to 11 a.m. are for veterans and active military.
services.hours: Wednesday and Thursday, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents; bring ID.

steps: Visit during hours with your ID.

services.name: FISH Fairborn
services.description: Food pantry for Fairborn and Bath Township.
services.eligibility: Fairborn and Bath Township residents; proof of residency and valid ID.

steps: Visit during hours with ID and proof of address.

services.name: Yellow Springs Community Food Pantry
services.description: Food pantry for Yellow Springs and Clifton, at Central Chapel Church.
services.hours: Second and fourth Thursdays, 2 to 4 p.m.
services.eligibility: Yellow Springs and Clifton residents.

steps: Visit during hours.

services.name: The Vineyard Church food pantry
services.description: Food pantry serving all of Greene County.
services.hours: Monday and Wednesday, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents; photo ID, plus a bill if you have a new address.

steps: Visit during hours with photo ID.
documents: A bill showing a new address, if it changed

services.name: Greater Dayton RTA
services.description: Buses in Montgomery County. Routes 1, 2, 4, 8, 19 and 22 stop at Sinclair. Riders with a disability can get a lower fare.
services.eligibility: Anyone; reduced fare with an RTA disability ID.

steps: Call RTA customer service for passes and student pricing.

services.name: RTA Project Mobility
services.description: Rides from your door for riders with a disability. Book a day ahead. Ask about a pass for the whole term.
services.eligibility: ADA paratransit certification.

steps: Call to get certified and book rides.

services.name: Greene CATS Public Transit
services.description: Public transit for Greene County.
services.eligibility: Anyone in the service area.

steps: Call to schedule a ride.

services.name: Legal Aid of Western Ohio
services.description: Free legal help for people with low income in western Ohio. They help with evictions and housing problems.
services.eligibility: Low-income residents of western Ohio.

steps: Apply online at legalaidline.org, or call the intake line.
Have any court papers or notices ready.
documents: Any notice or court papers you received

services.name: Lifeline phone or internet discount
services.description: Money off your phone or internet bill each month, if you qualify.
services.eligibility: Income at or below 135% of poverty, or receiving SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, federal public housing or a veterans pension. One per household.

steps: Apply online with the National Verifier. Or ask your phone company.
documents: Proof of SNAP, Medicaid or SSI, or proof of income

services.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
services.description: Free, confidential support any time. Call or text 988.
services.eligibility: Anyone.

steps: Call or text 988.

services.name: Dayton's Shelter for Men
services.description: A place to stay tonight for men in Montgomery County.
services.eligibility: Men who need a place to stay. Call first to check if there is room.

steps: Call 937-350-1335 to check if there is room tonight.
If you cannot get through, call 2-1-1 at 937-225-3000, any time.

services.name: Shelter for Women and Families
services.description: A place to stay tonight for women and families in Montgomery County.

organization.name: Society of St. Vincent de Paul, Dayton

services.eligibility: Women and families who need a place to stay. Call first to check if there is room.

steps: Call 937-461-7837 to check if there is room tonight.
If you cannot get through, call 2-1-1 at 937-225-3000, any time.

services.name: Daybreak
services.description: The Miami Valley's shelter for young people without a safe place to stay, with help finding a place of their own.
services.eligibility: Young people who are homeless, at risk of it, or moving from couch to couch. Call the hotline to ask whether you qualify.

steps: Call the 24-hour hotline, 937-461-1000.
Tell them where you are staying now and whether you are safe tonight.

services.name: Interfaith Hospitality Network of Greene County
services.description: Shelter and housing support in Greene County.

organization.name: Interfaith Hospitality Network of Greene County

services.eligibility: People in Greene County who need shelter. Call to ask about room and requirements.

services.name: Housing Solutions of Greene County
services.description: Housing help in Greene County.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents who need help with housing.

steps: Call 937-376-7810 and say what is going on with your housing.

services.name: YWCA Dayton crisis hotline and shelter
services.description: A safe place to stay and help for women and kids who are being hurt, threatened or followed.
services.hours: Crisis hotline open 24 hours, every day
services.eligibility: Women and children in Montgomery County at risk of harm. Shelter goes first to those at the highest risk.

steps: Call the 24-hour crisis hotline, 937-222-SAFE (7233).
If you are in danger right now, call 911.
how_to_use.what_to_expect: A hotline advocate talks with you about what is happening and what you need, and can arrange safe shelter.

services.name: Family Violence Prevention Center of Greene County
services.description: Help right away and a safe place to stay if someone has hurt you, for you and your kids.

organization.name: Family Violence Prevention Center of Greene County

services.hours: Crisis hotline open 24 hours, every day
services.eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence or sexual assault, and their children.

steps: Call the 24-hour crisis hotline, 937-372-4552.
If you are in danger right now, call 911.

services.name: Sinclair Counseling Services
services.description: Free, private counseling for Sinclair students. You can reach a counselor day or night.
services.hours: Counselor by phone 24 hours, every day
services.eligibility: Sinclair students.

steps: Call 937-512-3032. After hours and on weekends, choose the option to speak with a counselor.
Or fill in the appointment request on the Counseling Services page.
In an emergency, call or text 988.

services.name: Counseling and Wellness Services
services.description: Counseling for Wright State students. A $20 fee covers the whole semester; without it, sessions are $20 each.
services.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
services.eligibility: Currently registered Wright State students.

steps: Call 937-775-3407 or stop by 053 Student Union.
Ask about the $20 fee. It pays for all your visits that term.
After hours, call or text 988.

services.name: TCN Behavioral Health crisis line
services.description: Mental health and addiction care in Greene County, with a 24-hour crisis line for adults.
services.hours: Crisis line open 24 hours, every day
services.eligibility: Adults in Greene County. The main line for appointments is 937-376-8700.

steps: In a crisis, call 937-376-8701, any time, or call or text 988.
For an appointment, call 937-376-8700.

services.name: Samaritan Behavioral Health
services.description: Counseling and crisis care in Montgomery County, partly funded by the county mental health board.

location.address: 601 Edwin C. Moses Blvd., Fourth Floor

services.eligibility: People in Montgomery County who need counseling or crisis care.

steps: Call 937-734-8333 to ask for an assessment.
In a crisis, call or text 988, or go to the nearest emergency room.

services.name: Five Rivers Health Centers
services.description: Doctor and dentist visits at several sites, one of them in Greene County. You pay what you can.
services.eligibility: Anyone, insured or not. Fees are on a sliding scale based on income, and staff can help you sign up for Medicaid or other insurance.

steps: Call 937-281-6800 for an appointment.
Bring proof of income if you want the sliding-scale fee.
documents: Proof of income, for the sliding-scale fee

services.name: Community Health Centers of Greater Dayton
services.description: Primary care whether or not you can pay. Fees are based on what you can pay.

organization.name: Community Health Centers of Greater Dayton

services.eligibility: Anyone, insured or not. Sliding-scale fees based on income.

steps: Call 937-586-9733 for an appointment.
documents: Proof of income, for the sliding-scale fee

services.name: Greene County Public Health
services.description: Public health services in Greene County, including WIC food help for parents of young children and testing.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents. WIC is for pregnant people and parents of children under five, with income rules.

steps: Call 937-374-5600 and ask for the service you need.

services.name: Free Ohio state ID card
services.description: A state ID card at no charge, for Ohio residents 17 and older who do not have a valid driver license.
services.eligibility: Ohio residents 17 or older without a valid driver license. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian along.

steps: Gather proof of your full legal name, date of birth, Social Security number, legal presence and Ohio address.
Save your spot in line online. Then go to any BMV license office.

services.name: OhioMeansJobs Montgomery County
services.description: Free help finding work, job training and career support.

organization.name: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services

services.eligibility: Anyone looking for work or training.

steps: Call 937-225-5627 or walk in.
Bring a resume if you have one; staff can help you write one if not.

services.name: OhioMeansJobs Greene County
services.description: Free help finding work, job training and career support.

organization.name: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services

services.eligibility: Anyone looking for work or training.

steps: Call 937-562-6565 or walk in.

services.name: Mobile hotspot kits
services.description: Borrow a mobile internet hotspot for three weeks, free with a library card.
services.eligibility: Anyone with a Dayton Metro Library card in good standing. One kit at a time.

steps: Get a library card if you do not have one.
Request a hotspot kit in the catalog or at any branch.
Questions: the Ask Me line, 937-463-2665.
how_to_use.what_to_expect: Loans are 21 days, renewable up to five times if no one is waiting. A lost or damaged kit has a replacement fee.

services.name: Sinclair Accessibility Services
services.description: Help for students with a disability, like more time on tests or help with notes.
services.hours: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
services.eligibility: Students with a health condition or disability that makes daily life or school harder. You need a note from a doctor or other expert.

steps: Start the online Accessibility Application.
Send a note from your doctor that says what your needs are.
A staff member will call you to set up the help you need.

services.name: Office of Disability Services
services.description: Help for students with a disability, like more time on tests.
services.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
services.eligibility: Wright State students with a disability. You sign up for this on its own, apart from getting into school.

steps: Fill out the form online.
Send a note from your doctor that says what your needs are.
Attend a College Accommodation Planning meeting.

services.name: TRIO Student Support Services
services.description: Free help to stay in school. You get tutors, help with the FAFSA, money for books and a laptop to borrow.

situations.label: First in family to attend college

services.hours: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
services.eligibility: Sinclair students who are citizens or green card holders and need help with school. You also need one of these: no parent with a four-year degree, a lower income, or a disability on file.

steps: Fill in the online SSS application.
Staff contact you to talk about what would help most.

services.name: Tutoring and Learning Center
services.description: Free one-on-one or group tutoring for over 200 courses, on campus or by Zoom.

location.address: Building 7, Room L07, library lower level

services.eligibility: Currently enrolled Sinclair students.

steps: Book through the online reservation form: one-hour sessions, up to two per course each week.
Say which topics you want help with.

services.name: Veteran and Military Center
services.description: A home base for students who served. Get help with the GI Bill, sign up for classes early and meet other vets.
services.eligibility: Students who served or serve now, in any branch, and their families.

steps: Stop by 131 Allyn Hall or call 937-775-5550.
To sign up for classes early, bring your DD214 or military ID.

services.name: Military-friendly education center
services.description: Help with classes, benefits and making friends, for students who served and their families.
services.eligibility: Students who served or serve now, and their families.

steps: Call 937-512-2586 or book an in-person or virtual appointment.

services.name: Berry Family Career Hub
services.description: Help to pick a major, write a resume, get ready for interviews and find a job.
services.eligibility: Wright State students.

steps: Log in to Handshake to book an appointment or search for jobs and internships.

services.name: PIPP Plus
services.description: Pay a set share of your income for gas and electric instead of the full bill, all year.
services.eligibility: For homes with a lower income that get gas or electric from a big power company. For one person, the limit is about $27,900 a year.

steps: Apply online at energyhelpohio.gov, or ask your local help agency.
You will also need to apply for HEAP.
how_to_use.what_to_expect: You pay 5% of your monthly household income for each of gas and electric (10% in an all-electric home, at least $10).

services.name: Community Action Partnership, Greene County
services.description: Help with utility bills in Greene County.
services.eligibility: Greene County households with lower income.

steps: Call 937-376-7747 to ask about utility help and how to apply.

services.name: Find child care with 4C for Children
services.description: Staff help you find child care that fits your schedule and budget, or you can search online.
services.hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
services.eligibility: Families in 15 southwest Ohio and Miami Valley counties, including Montgomery and Greene.

steps: Call 937-220-9660 and ask for 1330.
Or use the Request Help Finding Child Care form, or the online search.
Ask your county help office if the state can pay for some of your child care.

services.name: Gem City Diaper Bank
services.description: Diapers for families who need them.
services.eligibility: Families in need of diapers.

steps: Call 937-231-1716 to ask where to pick up diapers.

services.name: Share 121 Clothes Closet
services.description: Free clothing in Greene County.
services.eligibility: Anyone who needs clothing. Call for hours.

steps: Call 937-372-1594 for hours and location.

services.name: The Salvation Army, Xenia
services.description: Help with emergency needs in Greene County.
services.eligibility: Greene County residents in need. Call to ask what help is available now.

services.name: Free fitness and events in the MetroParks
services.description: Free outdoor classes, from yoga and tai chi to bootcamp, and free festivals, in parks across Montgomery County.
services.eligibility: Everyone. Many classes need no registration.

steps: See the schedule at metroparks.org/programs.
Bring water, and a mat for yoga.

availability.value: Most outdoor classes run in the warm months; check the schedule

services.name: Campus Recreation
services.description: Free for students: fitness center, pool, climbing gym, courts and group fitness classes.
services.eligibility: Wright State students.

steps: Activate your free student membership at the Campus Recreation desk.

services.name: YMCA Extra Hands membership help
services.description: Lower membership fees at the Y based on household income or circumstances.
services.eligibility: Based on need: household income or circumstances. The Y says no one is turned away for inability to pay, as funds allow.

steps: Download the Extra Hands application, in English or Spanish, or ask at Member Services.

services.name: Art for All free weekends
services.description: Three weekends a year, the whole museum is free to visit.
services.eligibility: Everyone.

steps: Just go on an Art for All weekend.

availability.value: 2026: March 7 and 8, August 29 and 30, November 14 and 15
